#multiple latent variables

SUMMERMODEL<-' risk =~a+b+c

# moderation analysis

parts:
riskc<-scale(semdata$risk,center=TRUE,scale=FALSE)

PSc<-scale(SUMMER_final$PS,center = TRUE,scale = FALSE)

You are storing the data in new objects, rather than as new columns in SUMMER, which is the data.frame you are telling lm() to look in. 

xz<-riskc%*%c(PSc)


These are univariate, don't use matrix multiplication, just the regular multiplication operator: riskc * PSc
regression1<-lm(MH~ riskc + PSc+xz+gender+age, data=SUMMER_final, missing= “FIML”)

lm() does not have a missing="FIML" option; that is a lavaan option.

parts:
riskc<-scale(semdata$risk,center=TRUE,scale=FALSE).

My point is that for lm() to find it in data=SUMMER_final, you should put it in there:

SUMMER_final$riskc <- scale(semdata$risk,center=TRUE,scale=FALSE)[ , 1]

speaking of xz,
xz<- riskc * PSc does not work.... how can I fix this?

The problem is that scale() always returns a matrix, so in the syntax above, I added the brackets to extract the first/only column, making it a vector.  Do the same for PSc, and elementwise multiplication should work fine.  Alternatively, you can just subtract the mean

SUMMER_final$riskc <- semdata$risk - mean(semdata$risk, na.rm=TRUE)

FYI, if your latent means were already fixed to zero, then the factor score estimates should have means that are effectively zero.  This might all be unnecessary extra work.


Can't we use semTools::indProd() for moderation in lavaan

Yes, to model a latent interaction directly via product indicators.  See the references on that help page for details.  Fawad's suggestion is probably preferable to using factor scores for numerous reasons:
  • Treating factor score estimates as known values in a subsequent analysis will give you deflated SEs and inflated Type I error rates.
  • Since the model for the factors did not include nonlinear effects, it will not preserve them in the factor-score estimates.  So if there is an interaction, your power will be deflated.
